And therfore al{{ls}}o that vvhich of thee {{ls}}hal be borne Holy, {{ls}}hal be called the {{ls}}onne of God. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=36}} And behold {{sup|‖}} Eli{{ls}}abeth thy co{{ls}}in, {{ls}}he al{{ls}}o hath conceiued a {{ls}}onne in her old age: and this moneth, is the {{ls}}ixt to her that is called barren: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=37}} becau{{ls}}e there {{ls}}hal not be impo{{ls}}sible vvith God any word. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=38}} And {{sc|Marie}} {{ls}}aid, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ At this very moment when the B. And vpon the Imber friday in Aduent.}}And {{sc|Marie}} ri{{ls}}ing vp in tho{{ls}}e daies, vvent vnto the hil countrie vvith {{ls}}peede, into a citie of Iuda. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=40}} and {{ls}}he entred into the hou{{ls}}e of Zacharie, and {{ls}}aluted Eli{{ls}}abeth. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=41}} And it came to pa{{ls}}{{ls}}e: as Eli{{ls}}abeth heard the {{ls}}alutation of {{sc|Marie}}, the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Iohn the Bapti{{ls}}t being yet in his mothers vvombe, reioyced and acknowledged the pre{{ls}}ence of Chri{{ls}}t and his mother.}}∷ infant did leape in her vvombe. and Eli{{ls}}abeth vvas repleni{{ls}}hed vvith the Holy Gho{{ls}}t: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=42}} and {{ls}}he cried out vvith a loude voice, and {{ls}}aid, ''{{sup|‖}} {{sc|Ble{{ls}}sed}} art thou among vvomen, and ble{{ls}}sed is the fruite of thy vvombe''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=43}} And vvhence is this to me, that the {{sup|‖}} mother of my Lord doth come to me? {{verse|chapter=1|verse=44}} For behold as the voice of thy {{ls}}alutation {{ls}}ounded in mine eares, the infant in my vvombe did leape for ioy. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=45}} And ble{{ls}}sed is {{ls}}he that beleeued, becau{{ls}}e tho{{ls}}e things {{ls}}hal be accompli{{ls}}hed that vvere {{ls}}pokē to her by our Lord. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=46}} And {{sc|Marie}} {{ls}}aid, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ MAGNIFICAT at Euen{{ls}}ong.}}∷ ''MY {{sc|Sovle}} doth magnifie our Lord''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=47}} ''And my {{ls}}pirit hath reioyced in God my Sauiour''.⊣

{{verse|chapter=1|verse=48}} ''Becau{{ls}}e he hath regarded the humilitie of his handmaid: for behold from hence forth '' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Haue the Prote{{ls}}tants had alwaies generations to fulfil this prophecie? or do they call her ble{{ls}}sed, that derogate what they can from her graces, ble{{ls}}sings, and al her honour?}}∷ ''al generations {{sup|‖}} {{ls}}hal call me ble{{ls}}sed''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=49}} ''Becau{{ls}}e he that is mightie hath done great things to me, and holy is his name''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=50}} ''And his mercie from generation vnto generations, to them that feare him''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=51}} ''He hath {{ls}}hewed might in his arme: he hath di{{ls}}per{{ls}}ed the proude in the conceit of their hart''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=52}} ''He hath depo{{ls}}ed the mightie from their {{ls}}eate, and hath exalted the humble''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=53}} ''The hungrie he hath filled vvith good things: and the riche he hath {{ls}}ent away emptie''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=54}} ''He hath receiued I{{ls}}rael his childe, being mindeful of his mercie'', {{verse|chapter=1|verse=55}} ''As he {{ls}}pake to our fathers, to Abraham and his {{ls}}eede for euer''.<noinclude>{{rh|||And}}</noinclude>
